tieu_de: BIOGRAPHY OF VENERABLE MASTER HSUAN HUA
tom_tat: On March 17, the Year of the Horse (1918), Venerable Master Hsuan Hua was born into a Bach family, in a small village in Songcheng County, Jilin Province, Northeast China.
noi_dung:
BIOGRAPHY OF VENERABLE MASTER HSUAN HUA

SHI HENG TUNG

• * CHILDHOOD

On March 17, the Year of the Horse (1918), Venerable Master Hsuan Hua was born into a Bach family, in a small village in Songcheng County, Jilin Province, Northeast China.

As soon as he was born, he suffered for three days, feeling sorry for the Sentient Beings in the Saha world who suffered so much. At the age of 11, seeing a dead baby in the desert, he was somewhat awakened and wanted to leave family life and practice religion to solve the great problem of life and death.

At the age of 12, he began to repent of all his mistakes with his two parents, planning to repay his filial piety. He bowed to his parents every day. After that, he felt that bowing to his parents was not enough, he bowed to Heaven and Earth, the King, and the Master. He still feels it's not enough. Therefore, gradually He bowed to all Sentient Beings. He bowed morning and afternoon, more than 380 times, 5 times a day. He bowed to the wind, rain, and snow, hoping that through his bowing he would transform bad people into good people; I hope that bowing will bring peace to this chaotic world.

At the age of 15, he took refuge with the Venerable Thuong Tri at Tam Duyen Pagoda. Officially a Buddhist who has taken refuge in the Three Jewels. He is close to Venerable Thuong Nhan. At the age of 17, he only attended school for two and a half years. Because he achieved single-mindedness, he read it once and immediately memorized it. Thanks to that, he was proficient in the Four Books, the Five Classics, the Hundred Schools of Chu Tu, Medicine, Bodi, Astrology, Physics, and other worldly academic fields.

At the age of 16, he began preaching the Dharma Jewel Platform Sutra, Diamond Sutra, Amitabha Sutra, and explaining Buddha Dharma to illiterate people. At the age of 18, his mother fell ill. He dropped out of school and stayed at home to take care of him. Because He clearly knew the difficulties caused by not having a good education, He established a free class, teaching more than 30 poor children, from morning to night without stopping.

During his school years, he also participated in many charity associations, such as the Buddhist Association, the Ethics Association, the Charity Association, and the Association to encourage quitting drinking and smoking; Encourage giving up bad habits and doing good deeds. He practiced Bodhisattva conduct, vowing to save all living beings.

---o0o---

tom_tat: At the age of 19, his mother, Ho Thai, passed away. On April 8, the day Buddha was born, he bowed to Venerable Tri Nhan at Tam Duyen Pagoda and asked to become a monk. The Venerable received the novice ordination, his dharma name was An Tu,...
noi_dung:
* MONASTIC ORDINATION

At the age of 19, his mother, Ho Thai, passed away. On April 8, the day Buddha was born, he bowed to Venerable Tri Nhan at Tam Duyen Pagoda and asked to become a monk. The Elder monk ordained the novice ordination, his dharma name was An Tu, his dharma title was Do Luan. He asked for advice from the Venerable Thuong Nhan, abbot of Tam Duyen pagoda. When Venerable Hu Van taught him the Dharma, he was given the Dharma name Hsuan Hua.

During the three years he became a monk, he lived in a simple hut next to his mother's grave. People call him Bach Hieu Tu (filial son of the Bach family).

On June 19, the birthday anniversary of Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara, he made 18 great vows before the Buddhas. His life was the living practice of these 18 great vows.

"Bowing my head to pay homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions and the Tripitaka Dharma of the past, present, and future, along with the Sages and Sangha, I only wish to prove to my disciples the Dharma name Thich An Tu, from the Dharma Luan, that I now develop my mind not for the sake of praying for blessings in the Heavens, Humans, Sravakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and even Bodhisattvas of the right vehicle, only following the supreme vehicle to develop the mind of Bodhi. I vow that together with Sentient Beings in the entire Dharma world, they will all attain the state of Supreme Perfection at the same time. sense.

1. I vow that for the sake of all the Bodhisattvas in the uttermost reaches of space, throughout the dharma realm, in all three lives of the past, present and future, if there is one of them who has not yet achieved Buddhahood, then I have not yet attained Enlightenment.

2. I vow that for all the Pratyekabuddhas in the uttermost reaches of space, throughout the dharma world, in all three lifetimes, if there is even one of them who has not yet achieved Buddhahood, then I have not yet attained Enlightenment.

3. I vow that for the sake of all the Shravakas in the uttermost reaches of space, throughout the dharma world, in all three lifetimes, if there is even one of them who has not yet achieved Buddhahood, then I have not yet attained Enlightenment.

4.I vow that for the sake of all beings in the Heavens in the three worlds, if there is even one person who has not yet achieved Buddhahood, then I have not yet attained Enlightenment.

5. I pray that for all human beings, in the worlds of the ten directions, if there is even one person who has not achieved Buddhahood, then I have not yet achieved Enlightenment.

6.I pray that for humans, gods, and all Asuras, if there is even one person who has not yet achieved Buddhahood, then I have not yet achieved Enlightenment.

7.I pray for all animals, if there is even one who has not yet achieved Buddhahood, then I have not yet achieved Enlightenment.

8.I pray for all hungry ghosts, if there is even one who has not yet achieved Buddhahood, then I have not yet achieved Enlightenment.

9.I pray for all Sentient Beings in hell, if there is even one who has not achieved Buddhahood, then I have not yet attained Enlightenment.

10.I pray that all the Gods, Humans, Asuras, insects, even spiritual beings such as Dragons, Demons... have taken refuge with me. If there is anyone who has not achieved Buddhahood, then I have not yet attained Enlightenment.

11.I vow to bring all the blessings I deserve, ask for Dedication of Merit, alms, and offerings to all Sentient Beings.

12.I vow to take full responsibility for all the sufferings of Sentient Beings in this dharma world.

13.I vow to create countless incarnations to transform all Sentient Beings who do not have faith in the Buddha Dharma, causing them to abandon evil deeds and do good deeds, repent of all their sins, take refuge in the Three Jewels, and ultimately become Buddhas.

14.I pray that all Sentient Beings, when they see my face and hear my name, will develop the mind of Bodhi and quickly attain Buddhahood.

15.I vow to wholeheartedly respect the precepts established by the World-Honored One. Pray to practice eating one meal a day at noon.

16.I vow to enlighten all sentient Beings, taking care of all their abilities.

17.I vow to practice so that in this life I can have the five eyes, six powers, and come and go freely.

18.I pray that all the vows I have made will be fulfilled.

Last:

Sentient Beings do not hold back, vowing to save all.

Defilements are endless, vows are completely ended.

The Dharma has no quantity, all vows to practice.

Buddhism is incomparable, vows are fulfilled.

---o0o---

tom_tat: Venerable Master Hsuan Hua had chivalry and compassion from childhood. He could not bear to see others suffer. Therefore, He vows to endure all suffering for Sentient Beings. He cured countless people suffering from…
noi_dung:
* TREATMENT OF MIND ILLNESS

Venerable Master Hsuan Hua had chivalry and compassion from childhood. He could not bear to see others suffer. Therefore, He vows to endure all suffering for Sentient Beings. He cured countless people suffering from severe and strange diseases. Diseases that have no cure, such as plagues, haunted diseases, diseases caused by karma...

The monk said: "This is not because I have any special ability or magical powers. has any miraculous use. This is the strength of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. When the wish is sincere, it will receive the response of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas."

While using the blessing power to heal everyone, He explained to them the main meaning of the blessing power: "You should not only know how to look for gia __ outside, but first prepare yourself for yourself, then you can prepare everyone. That is the true meaning of blessing."

Why don't we get inspiration when chanting sutras, reciting mantras, or reciting the Buddha's name? Because we were not honest, we lied. You are the truth. If people do not lie, then all their words will be effective. If they call Heaven, Heaven immediately responds, calls the earth, and the land manifests. The Venerable said:

"I am a person without the gift of speaking, because I only know how to say the truth and say what people want to hear, especially in dispelling superstition. I am not afraid of offending people. If there is something that needs to be said, I will say it wherever I go. If there is something that does not need to be said, I will not say it. Simply because when we do not lie, every word, every word we say has boundless power and can heal. Heal the dangerous diseases of Sentient Beings as well as sentient beings. Like the storm that is supposed to come, a great earthquake will be prevented. Where there is no rain, there will be rain. The evil things that exist will be made to disappear, and the good things that do not exist will be made manifest. Natural inspiration will flow and immediately respond to everyone's wishes. Wherever the Truth is, there will be all kinds of Dragons, Devas and Angels to protect. Wherever the Truth is, all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas will come to protect it."

---o0o---

• * PROPAGATION OF THE Dharma

In 1948, the Venerable went to Hong Kong to spread the Dharma. In 1962, he accepted a request to go to the United States, where he made a great vow to propagate Buddhism, translate Sutras, and educate. He also established Bodhimanda, accepted disciples, established Principles, and laid the basic foundation for spreading Buddhism in the West. The Venerable often said:

“I can go a day without eating, but I cannot waste a day without explaining Buddhism.” – "As long as I have a little breath left, I will still preach the Dharma." – "I will preach the Dharma, even if many people or only a few people listen. Even if only one person comes, I will still preach. Even if no one comes, I will still preach for ghosts and gods to listen."

The Venerable's life's deeds are words and deeds, corresponding everywhere, at all times. That is the truest expression of the Dharma that he spread.

---o0o---

tom_tat: He lived next to His mother's grave for three years. To his parents, he is a filial son. Throughout his life, He always respected the elderly, loved children, and had compassion for Sentient Beings. Seeing water…
noi_dung:
* Dharma Legend

He lived next to His mother's grave for three years. To his parents, he is a filial son. Throughout his life, He always respected the elderly, loved children, and had compassion for Sentient Beings. Seeing that China was facing many disasters during the war, he did not give up his civic duty as a Chinese person. During more than 30 years in America, he voluntarily worked for the benefit of America, while still firmly maintaining his Chinese nationality. He is completely loyal to both countries.

He is very simple in using clothes, food, all personal belongings... to save energy for the whole world. He used the same pair of shoes for more than 30 years. He didn't have many clothes. When eating, if a grain of rice fell on the floor, he immediately picked it up and ate it. When He drank water, He emptied the glass. He used the simplest food, just boiled, no need for oil or salt. For His own blessings, He asks for Dedication of Merit to be given to all Sentient Beings. He does not have any assets of his own, because he has donated to charity funds.

Never follow external appearances. He always humbles himself the lowest and last of everyone. He began practicing the practice of bowing when he was 12 years old. He bowed to everyone all day without getting tired. After arriving in America, He also bowed to His disciples. He bowed until his disciples were willing to teach Buddhism. He bowed until some disciples vowed to make a pilgrimage with three steps and one bow. He bowed until His disciples bowed to those who slandered Him. Whenever he went anywhere, he let his disciples go first. He wants to go last to everyone. When teaching the Dharma, he let his disciples preach first and he was the last to preach. He was also the one who prayed for his disciples to achieve Buddhahood before him. He vowed to be the last person in the Dharma world to achieve Enlightenment.

His appearance and majesty are very complete. In a dignified and gentle manner. Eyes always looking down, hands always clasped at chest level. A smile often shines on the lips. His appearance is very majestic. When someone comes into contact with Him, He is always courteous and kind.

He never wanted to bother others. He washed his own clothes and carried his own luggage. He did not want anyone to serve him, even when he was seriously ill and had to walk with a cane. Even in the last years of his life, when he had to use a wheelchair, he still insisted on being able to carry his bag on his shoulder or in his arms as he traveled by plane from one Bodhimanda to another to preach in very poor health. He said: “I want to stand on my own two feet and use my own strength. I don't want to depend on anyone.”

He remained in meditation day and night. When work came, he immediately responded and resolved it promptly and quickly. Once done, return to regular serenity. He handled countless tasks during the day naturally and comfortably. He said: "I neither recite sutras nor recite mantras. The simple thing is that I do not give rise to false thoughts." He worked in a state of single-mindedness. He immediately recognized and corrected the interpreter's mistakes when translating His words into English. He never forgot anything. He remembered all the names, family situations, temperaments, and habits of all his disciples without confusion. He even remembered exactly how many steps He took during the day.

During the many years he spread the Dharma in America, people called him the First High Monk in the world, the Supreme Man. Ji Ming College in Shandong, China wants to change its name to Hsuan Hua College. There was a teacher who proposed the establishment of the "Dharma Realm Dieu Giac Son Nguyen Rescue Association" to study his deeds. He said: “Don't learn from me. I have nothing worthy to to learn from. You should study and learn from all people, men, women, monastics, Lay Buddhists, the elderly, children, good people, evil people... take note of their entire lives, because in the future, thanks to these events, you can educate and help everyone. My morality is not enough to feel sympathy. My virtue is not enough to transform people. People like to label me with names that I don't want. I'm not a high monk or a noble person. I'm just an ordinary person, I like to call myself "The Walking Dead", "The Little Ant", "The Little Mosquito". It is suitable for everyone, for every time, for every place. The name is not worth anything, yet many people are attached to the name and tire themselves, while I am alive and after I die, I do not want people to pay attention to my name or build a memorial tower for me. I come from nothingness, I return to nothingness.

---o0o---

tom_tat: At Bodhimanda branches of the Dharma Realm Buddhist Association, there are Sutra teaching courses to help people realize the truth. Therefore, each Bodhimanda has a daily Sutra lecture program. “River water circulates every day…
noi_dung:
* VERBAL LECTURES

At Bodhimanda branches of the Dharma Realm Buddhist Association, there are Sutra teaching courses to help people realize the truth. Therefore, each Bodhimanda has a daily Sutra lecture program. “If the river water circulates every day, the stream of dharma in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas will also be preached day and night.” There was a time when the Venerable used a method called “Dharma of Contemplation to to develop wisdom capital ”. To guide the four monks. Buddhists can come here to visit Buddha Dharma, to practice teachings and take teaching exams. The Venerable regularly opens the class "Question parallel answer" to help his disciples open their own inherent wisdom.

Depending on the conditions, the Venerable often chooses appropriate topics to preach to those who want to listen. To the common people, he preached about fulfilling one's basic duties and obligations. To students, he preached filial piety, loyalty, decency, integrity, self-awareness, love for family and duty to the Fatherland. To teachers and principals, he preached about the method of education and the vocation of education. To politicians, he spoke about morality, integrity and love for the people as if they were his own children.

When accepting an invitation to preach the Dharma, the monk never wished to be known by everyone. Because the Venerable just wants to spread teachings to train people. He never just went far to preach the Dharma. Furthermore, he always took his disciples with him to learn strange things in foreign countries. The daily program of this tour group is very detailed. In addition to the two usual morning and evening meditation sessions and the midday ceremony at noon, there are also times for repentance ceremonies, chanting Sutras, listening to Dharma Talk, attending the ceremony of transmitting the Three Refuges and Five Precepts to Buddhists, attending Great Compassion Dharma Conferences, Shurangama Dharma Conferences... or interacting with Buddhists. Don't let a single moment go to waste. The Venerable said: "We are not a tour group , nor a Dharma propagation group. We are simply a group of people going to learn. We are not yet familiar with many issues, and we are not qualified to do Dharma propaganda. We are very happy to follow everyone, looking forward to learning from Venerable Venerables and Elders everywhere"

---o0o---

tom_tat: The monk came from China to Hong Kong and then from Hong Kong to the United States. He made a vow: "Train people, not build pagodas." He mainly trains living Patriarchs, living Arhats, living Bodhisattvas and virtuous…
noi_dung:
* ESTABLISHING BODHIMANDA

The monk came from China to Hong Kong and then from Hong Kong to the United States. He made a vow: “Training people, not building temples”. He ​​mainly trained living Patriarchs, living Arhats, living Bodhisattvas and living Buddhas. Therefore, going through many difficult conditions, he repaired and restored the existing facilities as Bodhimanda to teach the Dharma in a timely manner to Buddhists. He advocated performing the practice right at the formless Bodhimandas. Bodhimanda branches of the Dharma Realm Buddhist Association everywhere may not look like traditional Chinese monasteries on the outside, but people can recognize the Pure Land inside, once they have gone there and truly committed to practice. He also has Vow: “From small pagodas, build large pagodas”, and establish public Great Bodhimandas. Every time he finished setting up a Bodhimanda, he offered it to others. He once worshiped under the two Great Bodhimandas, the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas and the City of Dharma Realm, as well as the branch monasteries of the Dharma Realm Buddhist Association. He makes offerings to all Sentient Beings in the world. He welcomes everyone who comes to practice, regardless of nationality, race, age, locality... regardless of background, regardless of whether they belong to the Northern or Southern Buddhist tradition, He has Vow to protect him, as well as anyone who comes to Bodhimanda to truly practice. The Venerable said: "We are not the ones who turn the pagoda into a private home. People from ten directions can come to this Bodhimanda. Here we are always waiting for a highly virtuous person to be the Abbot. I am only a temporary caretaker. There is no Bodhimanda that belongs to me."

He also said: "Buddhism is a teaching about humans, a teaching about mind, a teaching about them birth and a teaching about the entire dharma realm. Buddhism is not a separate dharma. I also do not belong to any sect. Christianity, Judaism, Islam and all other religions are included in Buddhism. We always welcome all other sects to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas to celebrate their rituals. All followers of all other religions should practice compassion. It is the foundation of all religions to save the whole world. Everyone should help each other and work together to establish the first foundation for religious unity globally. Sentient Beings will have a place to worship and the war will end quickly.

---o0o---

• * ACCEPT DISCIPLES

The Venerable said: "The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is a place where dragons and snakes are mixed together, with enough every components. Some people practice earnestly, some do not. We should live mindfully in the Four Immeasurable Minds: Compassion, joy and equanimity. In particular, we should pay attention to those who are not yet perfect and do our best to transform them into good people."

---o0o---

tieu_de: RECEIVE MONASTIC DISCIPLES - BUT DO NOT REJECT ANY SENTIENT BEINGS
tom_tat: The Dharma circulates thanks to the Sangha, the Dharma must be transmitted to everyone. In order for the Dharma to have a solid foundation in the West, there must be people who have practiced the right path. Therefore, the Venerable set out a…
noi_dung:
RECEIVES ORDINATED DISCIPLES - BUT DOES NOT REJECT ANY SENTIENT BEINGS

The Dharma circulates thanks to the Sangha, the Dharma must be transmitted to everyone. In order for the Dharma to have a solid foundation in the West, there must be people who have practiced the right path. Therefore, the Venerable set a very strict requirement for everyone who wanted to follow him to become a monk and become a monk, which was to graduate from college and recite the Shurangama Mantra by heart. After becoming a monk, one must study the Shurangama Sutra, learn how to preach the sutra, preach the Dharma, learn the meditation method and learn how to be patient and endure hardship. Over time, the Venerable began accepting monks of all levels. As long as that person has a little bit of good roots, the Venerable will accept them when they have the intention to become a monk. He also accepts people up to 90 years old, as long as they have the enthusiasm to practice. He also accepted children 6-7 years old, helping them grow their good roots. He also accepted those who were disabled and did not have enough six senses, and created good causes to help them escape the consequences of the mundane world.

---o0o---

tieu_de: * SAVING ALL BUDDHIST GOODS - BUT WITHOUT CONTENDING FOR DISCIPLES
tom_tat: The trend among Buddhists today is to take refuge with many teachers, so the Venerable taught: "Just taking refuge with one teacher is enough. Don't take refuge with this teacher and then leave that one. You take refuge with too many teachers without listening to their teachings, then...
noi_dung:
* SOLD OUT OF STOCK BUDDHIST - BUT DO NOT COMPETE WITH DISCIPLE

The tendency of Buddhists today is to like to take refuge with many teachers, so the Venerable taught: "Only need to take refuge with one teacher is enough . Don't take refuge with one teacher and then abandon the other. You take refuge with too many teachers without listening to their teachings, which is useless. Not only does this cause discord among Dharma Masters when they compete for disciples, but It also has consequences for places where veteran Buddhists are confused and confused. This does not create new vitality for Buddhism, but on the contrary, it will cause Buddhism to become corrupt.

As long as people's hearts are sincere, the Venerable Sa74n is willing to teach the Three Refuges and the Five Precepts even when he is sick, he does not care about troubles. Even if only one person comes to ask for ordination, he is ready to perform the ordination ceremony.

There are a number of Venerable monks. Cao Tang has always vowed not to accept disciples, afraid that because he is busy with teaching responsibilities, he will hinder his own practice. The Venerable Master was not like that. He accepted all those with stubborn, wild temperaments and those whose personalities were very difficult to tame. He vowed that it would be better to give up his head, eyes, marrow, and brain than to refuse salvation to these people.

---o0o---

• * SET UP PRINCIPLES

"Everyone who comes to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas must follow a number of regulations. Dragons must also curl up to be able to fly up and spray rain at will. Tigers must also crouch to be able to catch the direction of the wind and accurately pounce on their prey." At Bodhimanda Dharma Realm Buddhist Association, everyone must strive to practice the three Principles and six principles set forth by the Venerable as a standard for practice. The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is the center of these Buddhist Associations.

---o0o---

tom_tat: As soon as the two sessions of chanting began in the early morning, every afternoon the four disciples had to personally reflect on the correct
noi_dung:
* THREE PRINCIPLES AND SIX PRINCIPLES

Three Principles:

Right at the beginning of the two chanting sessions in the early morning, every afternoon the four disciples had to reflect on themselves:

1.Even if it's cold to death, there's no destiny; Even if you starve to death, don't beg; Even if you die poor, you don't ask for help.

2. Depends on fate without changing; does not change but depends on fate.

3. Resolutely practice according to the three Principles. I vow to give up my life and body to fulfill the Buddha's work. You yourself are responsible for transforming your own karma. Viewing diligent practice is the monk's main career.

Six principles:

Right in the Truth to clarify the Reason. Clear reason means Truth. Practice, promote, and circulate the sect that the Patriarch has transmitted.

Ask yourself, are you really a person who doesn't compete? Ask yourself, are you truly a non-greedy person?

I wonder if I'm really someone who doesn't want anything? Ask yourself, are you truly an unselfish person?

Ask yourself, are you truly a person without self-interest? Wondering if I'm really someone who doesn't lie?

I wonder if I'm really a person who eats a meal?

Do I always wear my robe without leaving my body?

These are the traditions of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, no one can change them.

---o0o---

• * ALWAYS WEAR BODY robe

To comply with the precepts established by the Buddha and to protect the monks, the Venerable taught the monks to always wear robes and carry cushions, not to let these things leave their bodies. He taught us to eliminate the desire to use precious and beautiful clothes.

---o0o---

• * EAT ONE LUNCH A DAY

Eating a lot of food at many meals a day will increase greed, making it difficult to practice. According to the rules established by the Buddha, monks practice eating one meal at noon and using pearl bowls. Boiled vegetables and "Arhat soup" are good medicines to cure hunger and thirst. People should not eat too much, they should eat just enough. Don't be greedy to eat too much, don't want to eat delicious food, you will be free from greed.

---o0o---

• * SLEEPLESS NIGHTS

Sleeping too much and being lethargic causes ignorance to grow. The Venerable had practiced never lying down to sleep at night since he was young, so he encouraged his disciples to sleep sitting up, making their minds peaceful, light, and alert. Thanks to that, you can escape the temptation of the devil.

---o0o---

• * DO NOT KEEP MONEY

Money is the root of sin. People with money easily give rise to false thoughts. To ensure effective practice, the Venerable taught his disciples to follow the Buddha's rules and not keep money as their own. Monks are not allowed to accept personal offerings for themselves. The work of the monks is of a service nature. When you are sick or have something wrong with the Sangha, you can use the Sangha's funds for expenses. The monk said: "Whoever can keep the precept of not storing private money, then is a monk worthy of the pure merit field."

---o0o---

• * NO HIERARCHY CONCEPT

In every Bodhimanda, the four disciples live and practice together. Everyone fulfills their own duties in the joy of Dharma. There is no fame, no power, no salary, so there are no private efforts to compete for personal benefits. There is no position of Administrator or Abbot. Everyone is equal in their own role as temple owners.

---o0o---

• * STRICTLY WITHIN MEN AND WOMEN

Any time two people need to contact each other, whether by phone or exchanging letters, there should be at least two other people by their side. This principle applies to all four beings to ensure all causes and conditions to maintain pure morality and freedom from all desires. Daily work is not separate from meditation practice: meditation practice is not separate from daily work.

---o0o---

• * PRACTICE YOURSELF

Daily meditation practice includes: morning meditation, Buddha worship, reciting the Avatamsaka Sutra, before noon, bowing to repent of Great Compassion. Afternoon practice: listen to the Sutra lecture, recite the Heart Sutra. There are also separate rituals and Dharma conferences on anniversaries, Sundays of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, the Great Water and Green Dharma Conference... At all times, everyone, depending on their ability, contributes to the fields of education, translating scriptures, handling daily monastic work... Thus, time is not allowed to pass in vain.

---o0o---

• * EVERY BODHIMANDA IS A SCHOOL

Education is the foundation of all worldly and extra-worldly dharmas. There are countless Dharma methods, all vows to practice and learn. We are teachers and students at the same time, learning from each other. In the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, there is Duc Luong Primary School, Virtue Cultivation High School, Dharma Realm Buddhist University, and educational programs for monks and Lay Buddhists. Many Bodhimanda branches have Dharma classes on weekends or on Sundays.

---o0o---

• * VOLUNTEER TEACHING IS THE RULE

Professors voluntarily teach without salary and without strikes. The purpose of education is to clarify morality, not for fame and fortune. Use Confucianism curriculum for basic classes and Buddhism for disciples who have taken refuge. Through education, we will discover and train talented people to serve the interests of the whole world. The monk said: “A person who does not need money is a true person”.

---o0o---

• * MEN AND WOMEN STUDY SEPARATELY

Men and women are organized to study separately, so they can focus on their studies without distractions. Thanks to that, it is possible to prevent social diseases such as: men and women interacting too early, abortion, divorce, homosexuality... Those phenomena are completely prohibited here. The Venerable said: “Education is the essential foundation of national defense, can save the whole society and can completely solve all the world's problems.”

---o0o---

tieu_de: EDUCATION IN THE MONASTY IS KEY
tom_tat: Monks are responsible for being role models for all Sentient Beings, so they must train themselves and study Buddhism perfectly before they take on the job of teaching others. Therefore, the Venerable specially educates his disciples...
noi_dung:
EDUCATION IN THE MONASTY IS KEY

Monks are responsible for being role models for all Sentient Beings, so they must train themselves and study Buddhism perfectly before they take on the job of teaching others. Therefore, the Venerable especially educates his monastic disciples very seriously and has very high demands on them.

Depending on each person's ability, disciples are assigned to undertake tasks in order to learn more. Everyone gets the same opportunities. Teachers often give students direct and indirect teachings as well as necessary support.

Dharma teachers often give monks surprise tests, such as inviting people from all walks of life, in all countries to lecture on sutras, and open courses at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas or other Bodhimanda branches. The Venerable said: "Everyone needs to have a clear view of the truth in examining the dharma eye. If you recognize the Way, you should move forward. If it is not the Way, then you should retreat. Choose good dharmas to practice, eliminate the bad qualities in yourself. Everything is a test for yourself. If you have not recognized what your face was before birth, then you must try to start from the beginning."

Dharmas are inherently uncertain. A fixed dharma is a dead dharma. Human beings are living dharma, you should not get stuck in a path until it leads you into darkness.

The monk said: “You must yourself clarify wisdom and have confidence in yourself. Don't believe in me.”

The Venerable's style is very comfortable and democratic. He respected his disciples and never arbitrarily established precepts. When a disciple does something wrong. He recently issued timely regulations to protect diligent study.

The Venerable has an infinitely forgiving heart. No matter who makes a mistake, as long as they have the desire to repent, the Venerable is willing to forgive. Accepting self-compassion: Immediately admit your mistakes.

Discussion of others: Do not discuss other people's mistakes.

Forgiveness means self-forgiveness: Seeing other people's mistakes as your own.

The same name of great compassion: Called the same mind of great compassion of the Buddhas.

The monk blamed himself instead of blaming others. He took upon himself all the mistakes, confusion, karma, and bad habits of his disciples. He vowed to shoulder all karma.

View the education of novice monks as the foundation of the education of monks.

In the last years of his life, he wholeheartedly cared for the education of young monks and novice monks. He personally arranged teachers and class times. He personally transmitted the Fourty-Two Hand Eye Seal Dharma to the novice monks to practice. He devoted all his heart and soul to transmitting these two precepts, hoping that the fellow practitioners of the four groups, of this class of young monks from 6 to 17 years old, will soon become the bright suns of Buddhism, will spread infinite compassion, peace and happiness, and guide Sentient Beings to practice the Bodhisattva path, transforming the suffering of life and death.

First, he recited a passage of the Sutra from memory, then continuously preached verse after verse without looking at the Sutra text. He did not need to write anything down, he taught completely from his own nature so that everyone could understand. He used common language to explain the most profound meanings of the Sutras, with very practical examples that all classes could understand. * PRESENTATION OF THE DISEASE

Ordinary people get sick due to karma. They accept what they have done in the past. All their illnesses are caused by greed, anger, and ignorance. The Saint's illness is due to the power of prayer. They vow to replace the bad karma that Sentient Beings have created. Because Sentient Beings are sick, Bodhisattvas are sick, and the Saints have already transformed all three poisons.

He was not sick, but wanted to bear all the suffering for Sentient Beings, taking on all the diseases of Sentient Beings for himself, so His body showed symptoms of the disease, with the hope that Sentient Beings would, when they saw the illness, know the cause of the illness, and would be determined to practice.

To protect the disciples of the four groups in their practice. He went from one Bodhimanda to another. Journeys by car, amid unusually hot and cold weather, handling countless complex tasks, help others gain blessings to practice. That made Him exhausted.

Ten years ago, he became seriously ill because of overwork. This year His illness was so severe that He could not even walk up a flight of stairs. Even when the doctors diagnosed him with only one week left to live. The monk still refused to rest to find a cure. He still walked using a walking stick or sat in a wheelchair, continuing to go everywhere to preach the Dharma. For the past two years, he has been bedridden due to illness and yet he still teaches disciples everywhere by phone, or appears in their dreams to educate.

The Venerable Master has cured countless people's illnesses, why wouldn't he cure himself? It's not because He can't cure, but because He doesn't want to cure. In all his life, he had never done or thought anything for himself. Even when He was in extreme pain, He did not need help for Himself at all. Even when He passed away peacefully on July 6 of that year (1995), His illness and pain did not decrease at all.

He did not show signs, nor left behind miracles. He only told people great lessons about formation, existence, destruction, emptiness - birth, old age, sickness, and death.

This is truly a great lesson that the Venerable gave to his disciples on the path of practicing the Bodhisattva path. Since countless eons ago, Bodhisattvas have sacrificed countless bodies to save Sentient Beings. You completely think about everyone else and not yourself. Faced with these unbearable sufferings, one can continue to courageously move forward with steadfast faith, unyielding while cultivating the Bodhisattva path, courageously continuing the deeds of the ancients. That is the unmelting gold of the Venerable in the blazing furnace.

His entire life is a manifestation of the Avatamsaka Sutra. Chapter "The inconceivable Dharma Realm of the Buddhas", in the Avatamsaka Sutra, it is said that the World-Honored Buddhas have ten vast Buddha deeds:

"Buddhists, when the Buddhas entered Nirvana, countless Sentient Beings cried in pain and felt sorrow and suffering. The field of immeasurable blessings has now completely disappeared. Therefore, to make Sentient Beings love and admire them, they do Buddhist work.

Even though the Buddhas and World-Honored Ones entered Nirvana, because of Sentient Beings, they continued to farm fields of inconceivable blessings; cultivating the ultimate blessing, endless blessings; causing Sentient Beings to have full good roots and a full field of blessings.

VIEW THE SUTRA WITH GRATEFULNESS

When reading the sutras, post-learners should have the following state of mind: the three karma of mind, speech, and mind must be pure. When the above three karmas are settled, blessings and wisdom are complete.

So sit upright as if sitting before the Buddha. That is pure karma.

The mouth does not say wrong words, does not laugh or joke. That is pure speech karma.

The mind is not scattered, the mind is completely free of predestined conditions. That is pure mind karma.

When the mind is calm, the external environment calms down, that is a contract to realize the source of the mind, a wonderful entry into the Dharma. noi_dung:
SENTENCE-BY-SENTENCE COMMENTARY

(Explain each sentence)

Nam mô hắc ra đát na đá ra dạ da

Every day we still chant Namo Amitabha Buddha. Namo Original Master Shakyamuni Buddha. But do you know what Nam - mo means? Probably very few people know. A few years ago, I once posed this question in a Dharma conference, but no one had a complete answer.

Nam - mo, transliteration of the word Nama from Sanskrit. Chinese translation is "Refuge"; also translated as "Respecting the head and the head". Meaning: "I would like to bring my entire life to rely on the Buddhas." My own ego is no more. But I would like to offer my entire life to the Buddhas. If the Buddhas let me live, I will live; tell me to die, then I die. I completely believe in Buddhas. That's called "Rule of life".

"Respect first" means to show utmost respect and reliance on the Buddha. That is the meaning of Nam - mo.

"Taking refuge" means bringing all your body and mind, bringing all your life back to rely on the Buddha.

Speaking in general. Namo black ra dat na stone ra da da means "Please take refuge in the boundless Three Jewels throughout the ten directions".

That is the essence of Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara. You should start a mind of Compassion and recite it. Although it is the essence of Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara, it also means taking refuge with all Buddhas in the ten directions, throughout all three lifetimes: past, present, and future. When you recite this mantra. Not only does it remind us to take refuge in the Three Jewels that permanently abide in the boundless and endless ten directions, but it also makes all sentient beings who hear this mantra also return to take refuge and pay homage to the ten directions and three lifetimes that permanently abide in the Three Jewels.

Do you know what the Three Jewels are? These are Buddha treasure, Dharma treasure and Sangha treasure. You should know that Buddha is the most noble in this world. Likewise, the Dharma says and

Sangha treasure is the noblest and most precious thing. Not only is it noble in the world, but it is also noble in realms beyond this world, even in the heavens of neither perception nor non-perception. There is nothing more noble than the Three Jewels in Buddhism. Among the ten dharma realms, the Buddha realm is the highest. Therefore, we need to reverently worship and believe in the noble Three Jewels, develop solid and deep faith, without the slightest doubt.

Some people will ask: What is the benefit of taking refuge in the Three Jewels? At the very least, when you take refuge in Buddha, you will no longer fall into hell; When you take refuge in the Dharma, you will no longer fall into the realm of hungry ghosts; When you take refuge in the Sangha, you will no longer be reborn as an animal. These are the basic principles of taking refuge in the Three Jewels.

But once you have taken refuge, you must voluntarily and diligently practice good deeds in accordance with the Buddha's teachings to be worthy of being called taking refuge. If you still maintain the same old habits such as killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, addiction and doing everything you like to satisfy the five desires, then you cannot avoid falling into the 3 evil realms (preta, hell, animals). Because in Buddhism there is no tolerance. You cannot say: "I have taken refuge in the Buddha, taken refuge in the Dharma, and taken refuge in the Sangha, so I will never fall into hell, hungry ghosts, or animals again. So I have the right to do whatever I want..."

You must change and transform all your bad habits and actively practice good deeds, and definitely never do evil deeds again. If you continue to do evil deeds, you will immediately fall into hell.

Buddhism is not like paganism. They declared: "The most important thing is faith. If you have faith, even if you do evil deeds, you can enter heaven. On the contrary, if anyone lacks faith, even if they try to do good deeds, they will fall into hell."

If you believe in Buddha and still create bad karma, you will definitely fall into hell. Even if you don't believe in Buddha, but still try your best to do good deeds, you will still go to heaven. Buddhism never deceives people by saying: "If you believe in Buddha, everything will be as you wish." On the contrary, if you believe in Buddha but still refuse to give up evil deeds, you will still fall into hell.

"Alright". You wonder again: "If you already believe in Buddha but still fall into hell without believing, then why do you have to take refuge in the Three Jewels?"

Truly taking refuge in the Three Jewels means giving up evil deeds, returning to the good path, and correcting all mistakes. Like a person who is reborn with a new name, from now on he only does purely good deeds. Don't do bad things anymore. Only then can practical benefits be achieved. That's why the mantra: Namo hac ra dat na kick ra da da means: "Take refuge in the infinite Three Jewels throughout the ten directions".

When you recite this mantra, it can also help eliminate your evils. When you encounter an obstacle, you should often recite: Namo black ra dat na kicks the stomach and skin, then the obstacle will be immediately eliminated. Big accidents will turn into small accidents, and if you have a small accident, they will be wiped out. This mantra is called the "Elimination of disasters" and is one of the five sets of mantras to protect demons.

Namo black ra dana stone ra da da is also called "Tang beneficial dharma". This means that up to now, you have planted many good roots, and still recite this mantra often, your good roots will grow many times over, and the benefits will be incalculable. So this mantra is called "Increasing Benefits Dharma".

You can recite the entire Great Compassion Mantra, or just recite this first mantra: Namo ra dat na kick ra da da is "Accomplishment of dharma", no matter what you want, your wishes and desires will be fulfilled as you wish. If you don't have a son and want to have a son, recite Namo tac ra dat na kick ra da da and you will give birth to a son. But you must recite with a sincere mind, not just for a day or two, but continuously for at least three years. If you don't have a good friend, but want to meet one, recite Namo hap ra dat na kick ya da and you will immediately meet a good friend. If you can recite the entire Great Compassion Mantra, that's great. If not, just reciting the first sentence Namo ra dat na kick ra da da, will also achieve inconceivable merits.

This mantra is also known as "Goods serve the Dharma". The power of that mantra can subdue demons and pagans when they hear this mantra.

However, this mantra is not a "Dharma Summons". When you recite a mantra in the "Dharma Summons", all kinds of demons and demons from everywhere will appear and can capture or control them.

Therefore, this mantra "Namo black rat dat dat" has a very powerful function, which cannot be measured. If we talk about the details, it's impossible to get to the bottom of it.

In short, in the sentence Namo hac ra dat na kick ra da da, Nam mo means "to respect the head". Black ra da na means "to tell". Kick out the stomach means "Three". Da means "Ceremony".

The meaning of the whole sentence is: "Please take refuge with all your body, mind, and life and pay homage to the limitless and boundless Three Jewels in all ten directions, throughout all three lifetimes." We must bow our heads and pay homage to the Three Jewels.

Why is it called endless and boundless? Because the Buddhas of the past are infinite. The Buddhas in the present time are infinite. The Buddhas of the future are infinite. Therefore, the Three Jewels are boundless and endless.

2. Nam mô a rị da

Namo as explained above, means "to take refuge in one's body, mind, and life, to pay respects and study the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas".

A ri means "Saint". It means a person who is far away from all evil. So Namo A ri da means paying homage to the Saints who have left all unwholesome dharmas.

3. Bà lô yết đế thước bát ra da

Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara means "contemplation" in the title Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Also translated as "light" from the title Vairocana (Bhikkhu - Lo - Gia - na) means Light of Transformation - Light shining everywhere. Also translated as: "Department of observation" means the realm to be contemplated, to be observed. Ruler bowl ra da means "freedom".

The whole meaning of the sentence is to contemplate and observe widely and freely. That is the meaning of the title Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara, Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara. It means observing and listening to sounds in the world to be saved freely.

4. Bồ đề tát đỏa bà da

Everyone knows that Bodhi comes from the Sanskrit word Bodhi. Means Enlightenment.

Tat reda means "to save" and to overcome (the ocean of suffering) as well as bring others to overcome (the ocean of suffering) to the shore of liberation.

Bodhisattva reda ba da means a Bodhisattva who has attained enlightenment and liberation and helps all Sentient Beings to become enlightened and liberated like himself.

Ba da means "to pay homage".

Da means kowtow. Bowing to whom? Paying homage to the Bodhisattvas who have already achieved enlightenment and liberation for themselves, they also help others achieve enlightenment and liberation.

This mantra refers to Bodhisattva Bodhisattva Bat Khong Quyen Sach suppressing the great army. It means that when you chant this mantra, Bodhisattva Bat Khong Quyen Sach brings the soldiers of heaven to protect you.

5. Ma ha tát đỏa bà ha

Ma - ha has 3 meanings: Dai: big; Many: many; and Thang: perfect.

Ma-ha means Great: that is, only for people who develop a broad Bodhi mind.

Ma - ha means Da: meaning only quantity. There are many people who develop bodhicitta.

Ma-ha means Victory: it refers to those who have developed a great mind of bodhichitta and have reached the point of complete achievement, receiving many outstanding benefits.

The meaning of the word Tat - reda in this mantra is not the same as the meaning in the sentence above. In the above mantra, Tat-reda means "transcend" - to cross over to the other shore. Means liberation. And in this mantra. Tat - reda means "strong man" who is courageous and fearless. It also means "Diligence", someone who practices very diligently.

Ba - Da Han translates as "Praying to others" meaning: "I bow my head to pay homage to the great Bodhisattvas, who are very brave, very diligent, never afraid, and vow to develop Bodhisattva before these Bodhisattvas."

The great Bodhisattvas have enlightened and liberated themselves and have also vowed to help countless other Sentient Beings become enlightened and liberated like themselves.

6. Ma ha ca lô ni ca da

Ma-ha has 3 meanings: big, many and superior as explained above.

Ca – lô Hán dịch là “Bi”.

Ni-ca means "Mind".

Combined, Ma ha ca lo ni ca means "Great compassion".

Da means to pay homage, as explained above. The entire mantra Ma ha ca lo ni ca da means: "Bow your head to pay homage to the Great Compassion Mantra of Da-la-ni mind."

7. Sentence

An means "Original Mother", the "Uncle Mother" of all mantras; She is also the "Buddha mother" of all Buddhas.

The mother of the Buddhas means the mother of the mind source of all Sentient Beings, because the mind source of Sentient Beings inherently has all wisdom, often giving birth to good dharmas, so it is called "Original Mother".

Through the power of the mantra, the ten dharmas are revealed.

The first method is "Self": it is the source, giving birth to all syllables.

The second is “Owl”. In scriptures or in mantras, “Owl” means a sentence.

The third is "Contemplation": to contemplate, to observe, to apply the power of contemplation to practice.

Fourth is "Tri": wisdom, using the sword of wisdom to cut off all afflictions. Wisdom is the method that flows from Prajnaparamita, which is the most complete wisdom. And "contemplation" is derived from the Paramita Meditation method.

Fifth is "Practice": meaning to practice, to practice according to the Dharma.

The sixth is "Vow": meaning it is necessary to make a vow, to practice according to the true Dharma.

Those who perform the ordination ceremony also recite this mantra. This means that becoming a monk and practicing Buddhism will be fulfilled and fulfilled.

At this point, the Great Compassion Da La Ni Sutra and the Great Compassion Mantra have been explained. Now I have also explained all forty-two hand-eye mudra dharmas, which is the second part of the Great Compassion Da La Ni Sutra. The next part is the science of practice, the method of practice, I won't mention it anymore.

Last year, some disciples wished to listen to the Great Compassion Mantra. You have been listening to the lecture for nearly a year now. This Dharma conference is considered a complete accomplishment.

I pray that whatever you set your mind to practice will be as you wish, everything will be Pada da ta ta ha, that is, the fulfillment of your wishes. Each person has different aspirations, so the achievements are not the same, but they are all perfect.

May all Buddhists who have the opportunity to hear this Sutra of Great Compassion Da La Ni soon achieve Buddhahood, because this is the Vow of those who deeply believe in the Buddhas.

Once you have attained Buddhahood, everything is "satisfactory".
